desc:
An ecommerce conversion audit is a written review of your store funnel with a ranked fix list, so you know what to change first. Ecom Swift LLC walks through your store as a first-time shopper would and reads your analytics to find where people leave.

## Why a store needs an audit before more traffic

Sending more visitors to a store with leaks only increases the number of people who leave. Many owners respond to flat sales by buying more ads or redesigning the home page, when the real problem may sit in a product page, a shipping message or a slow phone layout. An audit finds the actual cause so you spend effort where it counts.

An outside reviewer also sees what you no longer notice. After months of looking at your own store, the confusing label or missing size chart feels normal. A fresh set of eyes does not.

## What is a conversion audit?

A conversion audit is a structured review of every step a shopper takes: landing page, collection, product page, cart, checkout and thank-you page. For each step we ask whether a stranger can understand the offer, trust the store, find what they need and complete the next action without effort.

The result is a report, not a vague opinion. It contains screenshots, plain notes and a list of fixes ranked by how much they are likely to matter and how hard they are to do.

## How the audit helps your results

Conversion work succeeds when you fix the biggest problems first. Without a ranked list, owners tend to start with the changes that are fun, like colors and banners, instead of the ones that matter, like unclear shipping costs. A ranked list puts quick wins first and larger projects in order.

Your analytics add evidence. A page with many visitors and many exits deserves attention before a page that few people see. We use that data to separate real drop-off points from guesses.

## What a thorough audit covers

- First impression: whether the home page explains what you sell within a few seconds.
- Navigation and search: whether shoppers can reach a product in a few taps.
- Collection pages: filters, sorting, product cards and image quality.
- Product pages: photos, titles, price display, variants, descriptions and buy button.
- Trust items: policies, contact details, reviews and payment icons.
- Cart and checkout: steps, field count, shipping costs and payment options.
- Mobile and desktop side by side, since problems often appear on only one.
- Drop-off points seen in your analytics from page to page.
- Page speed notes that affect how fast each step loads.
- A list of test ideas, so later changes can be measured.

## How we carry out the audit

We first look at your store without any special tools, exactly as a new visitor would, on a phone and a computer. Then we read your analytics to see where visitors leave and how mobile and desktop differ. We compare what we saw with what the numbers show, because the two often explain each other.

You receive a written report with screenshots, short explanations and a ranked fix list. Use it as a plan for yourself or your developer, or order the fixes from us as a separate job.

The Basic package reviews home, product, cart and checkout and names the biggest fixes. The Standard package is deeper, with mobile and desktop comparison, analytics drop-off review and speed notes. The Premium package covers the whole funnel, adds ranked test ideas, compares your store with two competitors and ends with a walkthrough call. Add-ons include a recorded video walkthrough and heat map setup.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Share your main goal, such as more orders or higher order value.
- Tell us what you have already tried.
- Give us your analytics access if you have it.
- Fix the ranked list from the top, not from the easiest item.
- Review the results again after the changes are made.

**Avoid:**
- Redesigning before you know what is wrong.
- Copying a competitor's layout without knowing whether it works for them.
- Making many changes at once, which hides which one helped.
- Treating the report as a one-time document and never revisiting it.
- Ignoring mobile because the store looks fine on a laptop.

## Who this is for

An audit suits a store with steady traffic and flat orders, an owner preparing for a busy season who wants the biggest problems fixed first, and a business that has hired a developer and wants a clear, prioritized brief to hand over.

## What we need from you

Send your store address and a short note on your goals. If you use analytics, give us viewer access as a team or collaborator user. We never need passwords, and a store without analytics can still be audited from the shopper side. We reply with a short checklist after you order.
